failure_analysis.root_cause: Substrate (L-arginine) depletion. Initial substrate 75 µM depleted to 0 µM because NO secretion consumes substrate faster than CSF diffusion replenishes it. Without substrate, eNOS enzyme cannot produce NO.
failure_analysis.mechanism_vs_implementation: MECHANISM FAILURE — the substrate consumption rate is a real biological constraint, not a model bug. Endothelial cells in CSF (low L-arginine compared to blood) will face this constraint.

repair_pipeline_per_Article_XXXVI_§4.diagnosis: Substrate depletion. The model assumed CSF L-arginine ~75 µM (blood-like) and passive diffusion. In reality, CSF L-arginine is ~10-20 µM (lower than blood), and the catheter surface has limited diffusion access. The substrate consumption rate exceeds the replenishment rate.
repair_pipeline_per_Article_XXXVI_§4.one_repair_attempt: Add active substrate replenishment mechanism: (a) L-arginine reservoir in catheter wall, slow-release; OR (b) co-culture with cells that synthesize L-arginine; OR (c) use a NO donor compound (DETA-NONOate) instead of enzymatic production.
repair_pipeline_per_Article_XXXVI_§4.repair_choice: (c) NO donor compound (DETA-NONOate) — chemical NO release, no substrate dependence. Published half-life ~20h at 37°C, can be embedded in catheter polymer.
repair_pipeline_per_Article_XXXVI_§4.repair_falsification: NO release rate >= 1.0 pmol/cm²/s sustained for 30 days from DETA-NONOate-doped polymer
repair_pipeline_per_Article_XXXVI_§4.if_repair_fails: P-18 -> CEMETERY. Article XXXVI §4: repair budget = 1, second failure terminal.

R313_action: Execute repair attempt (c) — model DETA-NONOate NO release kinetics. If sustained >= 1.0 pmol/cm²/s for 30 days, P-18 repaired. If not, P-18 -> cemetery.
reusable_negative_knowledge_if_killed: Enzymatic NO secretion from living endothelial cells in CSF is substrate-limited. CSF L-arginine (~10-20 µM) is too low to sustain therapeutic NO secretion. Future NO-based anti-biofilm mechanisms should use chemical NO donors (DETA-NONOate, SNAP) rather than enzymatic production.
